newsitem.title: UK: Abbey National to show good operating growth.
newsitem.headline: Abbey National to show good operating growth.

text.p: Abbey National Plc, which kicks off the reporting season for British banks next Tuesday is expected to report some pressure on margins and only modest mortgage growth but operating profits will show good growth.
Abbey is among the major mortgage market players which has rejected the fight for volume and has sought to protect its margin, although volumes are thought to be picking up.

Abbey's first half profits are expected to have risen by over 20 percent to at least 675 million pounds but the comparison will be flattered by profits from its acquisition of the National & Provincial Building Society last year.
Dividend is expected to rise by over 20 percent to 10.5 pence per share from 8.7 pence last time.
Other areas of the business are thought to have done well, including insurance and consumer lending.
Its general insurance joint venture with Commercial Union is seen as an area of important growth, while life insurance and consumer credit should also post good growth.
On top of the operating performance, Abbey is expected by analysts to start showing the cost savings of the merger with N&P though there will be more of these in the second half.

Costs in the business may edge temporarily higher in terms of the cost/income ratio, though this is thought likely to be reversed in the second half, with the ratio again moving down towards the bank's target of 40 percent.
In terms of strategy, Abbey National chief executive Peter Birch, who retires next year, is likely to be questioned on further acquisitions.
Abbey missed out on buying Scottish Amicable earlier this year and later rebuffed a merger approach from National Westminster Bank.

It has bought financial sevices group Cater Allen but analysts may be looking to the bank to make a major purchase in its areas of diversification although Birch has made it clear that Abbey was unwilling to pay the high prices being asked.
Birch will also be asked about the mortgage market and is expected to be cautious about any pick-up in activity outside of the south-east of England.
